title: Multi-tenant Affinity & Noise Mitigation: Lab Procedures and Operator Checklist
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document describes a repeatable lab procedure and operator checklist for measuring, simulating, and mitigating multi-tenant noise and affinity interactions in the Redwood serving runtime. It is intended for runtime engineers, SREs, and performance analysts who run fidelity and cost experiments that require isolating or intentionally stressing cross-tenant interference.

Goals

- Provide a deterministic lab experiment template that reproduces common multi-tenant noise modes (co-located KV cache thrash, kernel contention, NUMA-induced memory pressure).
- Define measurable SLOs, dashboards, alert thresholds, and acceptance criteria for mitigation experiments.
- Equip operators with a step-by-step runbook to triage noise incidents and apply mitigations (affinity pinning, soft isolation, admission shaping).

Scope and non-goals

- Scope: experiments run on our staging GPU pool or dedicated lab cluster; tests target sequence lengths 64-4096, open-model variants (float16, q4_0), and mixed workload mixes (short chat requests, long completions, embeddings).
- Non-goals: this lab does not cover third-party accelerator integration (see team-wiki/third-party-accelerator-compatibility-and-dependency-matrix).

Key definitions

- Noise: performance variance introduced by other tenants or background processes (e.g., eviction sweeps, kernel uploads).
- Affinity: policy that ties a request class to a placement decision (GPU, NUMA node, kernel type).

Summary of approach

1) Controlled traffic generation: use the experimental traffic-replay harness to inject synthetic tenants with distinct traffic signatures.
2) Noise modes: run focused microbursts and slow-moving background loads simultaneously to recreate tail-latency spikes.
3) Observability: collect per-request timeline traces (request_id, kernel_id, kvcache_state, dispatch_slot) and aggregate into heatmaps.
4) Mitigation: iterate through affinity adjustments and admission shaping policies to measure SLO impact vs cost.

Test matrix (sample)

| Scenario | Primary metric | Secondary metrics | Description | Acceptance threshold |
|---|---:|---|---|---:|
| Baseline single-tenant | p95 latency (tokens/sec) | p99 latency, tail CPU/GPU occupancy | Warm cluster with only target tenant | p95 < 80ms for short requests |
| Co-located microburst | p99 latency | queue depth, kernel queue wait | Synthetic tenant sends repeated long completions | p99 < 400ms or < 2x baseline |
| KV-cache thrash | median throughput | kv cache miss rate, warmup time | Background tenants flush prefixes to evict KV cache | throughput drop < 20% from baseline |
| NUMA contention | p95 latency | host memory bandwidth, swap events | Large model variants placed across NUMA boundary | no swap events; p95 degradation < 15% |

Lab setup (hardware & software)

- Cluster: staging-gpu-pool-1 (4x A100:80GB nodes), dedicated switch VLAN for experiments.
- Images: runtime:release-2025-02, kernel-runtime:ci-20250210, observability-sidecar:0.9.
- Tools: traffic-replay (v0.7), trace-collector (v1.3), sample-analyzer (v2.0).
- Configs stored under s3://redwood-labs/mt-affinity-experiments/<run-id>/

Quick deployment commands

1) Provision a test namespace and node selector:
   kubectl create ns mt-affinity-lab-<run-id>
   kubectl label nodes gpu-01 node-role.kubernetes.io/affinity=experiment

2) Deploy runtime with debug flags and sidecars:
   kubectl apply -f runtime-debug-deployment.yaml -n mt-affinity-lab-<run-id>

3) Start traffic generators (example):
   ./traffic-replay --config examples/mt/microburst-mix.yaml --run-id <run-id> --target-endpoint https://staging-infer.redwood.internal/generate

Sample traffic config (examples/mt/microburst-mix.yaml)

---
primary_tenant:
  qps: 80
  seq_len: 128
background_tenant_1:
  qps: 20
  seq_len: 1024
background_tenant_2:
  qps: 5
  seq_len: 2048
mix_policy: random-weighted
---

Observability & metrics to collect

- Per-request span timeline (start/kernel-dispatch/kernel-complete/response-send).
- Kernel queue wait (ms), kernel execution time (ms), kvcache_miss boolean.
- Host-level: gpu_utilization, memory_bandwidth, cpu_iowait, dmesg errors.
- Aggregates: p50/p95/p99 latency per tenant, throughput, error-rate, cost-per-token estimate.

Dashboards and heatmaps

- Recommended dashboard panels: tenant-latency-by-severity, kernel-wait-by-kernel, kvcache-hitmap (prefix vs tenant), host-memory-bandwidth
- Heatmap recipe: bucket requests by kernel_id and time-of-day; overlay admission rates to identify correlation windows.

Operator runbook: triage and mitigation checklist

1) Detect: Alert fires when p99 latency increases by > 2x baseline or when kvcache_miss_rate > 30% sustained for 2m.
2) Verify: Confirm scope by comparing tenant traces; run trace-collector --run <run-id> --filter tenant=primary.
3) Isolate: Temporarily scale down noisy tenants: kubectl scale deploy background-* --replicas=0 -n mt-affinity-lab-<run-id>.
4) Quick mitigations (ordered):
   a. Apply soft affinity: runtimectl set-affinity --tenant primary --policy prefer-isolated-gpu
   b. Turn on admission shaping: runtimectl set-admission --tenant primary --max-concurrency 10
   c. Increase KV-cache allocation for primary tenant via placement hint: annotations: runtime.kvcache.size: "2GB"
5) Validate: Re-run traffic harness for 3x baseline window and confirm p95/p99 within thresholds.
6) Rollback if required: runtimectl rollback-affinity --to previous-config (keep run-id logged).

Mitigation experiments: parameter sweep and cost accounting

- Sweep parameters: affinity degree (none, soft, hard), admission threshold (5,10,20), kvcache allocation (512MB, 1GB, 2GB).
- For each configuration capture: run-id, cost-delta (estimated GPU-minutes), latency deltas, and false-positive impact on background tenants.

Example analysis snippet (sample-analyzer CLI)

./sample-analyzer summarize --run-id <run-id> --group-by affinity,admission --metrics p95,p99,kv_miss_rate --output s3://reports/mt/<run-id>.csv

Acceptance criteria for production rollout

- Primary tenant p95 under target by <10% compared to baseline while background tenant performance does not degrade >25%.
- No host-level swap or OOM during a sustained 30-minute test window.
- Cost delta acceptable per product policy: additional GPU-minutes < 12% for steady-state mitigation.

Postmortem & artifacts

- When an experiment identifies a regression or successful mitigation, attach artifacts to the experiment ticket: run-id, raw traces (trace-collector output), sample-analyzer CSVs, dashboard permalink.
- Follow incident review template: one-line summary, timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigation applied, and next steps.

Known limitations and caveats

- Lab clusters are smaller than production; noisy behaviour can amplify differently at scale. Always run a scaled smoke test in a larger staging pool prior to production rollout.
- Kernel-level behavior varies by architecture (A100 vs H100); include accelerator tag in all run metadata.

Ownership and contacts

- Owners: serving-runtime/perf-team (primary), eng-sre (on-call escalation).
- Escalation path: #runtime-perf (Slack) -> eng-sre pager -> oncall-engineer@redwood.ai

Appendices

A. Common mitigation commands
- runtimectl set-affinity --tenant <t> --policy prefer-isolated-gpu
- runtimectl set-admission --tenant <t> --max-concurrency <n>
- kubectl annotate deployment <d> runtime.kvcache.size=\"1GB\" -n <ns>

B. Example failure signature
- Symptom: sudden p99 spike correlated with kernel upload events and large KV miss ramps.
- Likely cause: background tenant performing long completions causing streaming kernel uploads that evict small KV prefixes.
- Short-term fix: soft affinity + increase kvcache allocation for affected tenant.

C. Lab checklist before test
1) Confirm runtime image version and kernel hashes.
2) Reserve GPU nodes and label them for experiment use.
3) Set observability retention to 60m for trace sampling.
4) Record baseline with no background traffic.

If you find gaps in playlists or tooling, open an experiment ticket and tag "runtime-affinity-lab".
